key_insight: RPG lets embodied agents improve robot execution without weight updates by iteratively reconstructing tasks, practicing in simulation, and upgrading a reusable skill/prompt system from failure feedback.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to cheaper, safer robot capability scaling by reusing offline data and simulator feedback instead of expensive end-to-end retraining.
method: Mine capabilities from offline datasets and turn them into practice tasks in simulation
Use execution feedback, simulator state, and dataset videos to diagnose failures
Retain better symbolic skills and prompt revisions after cross-task evaluation
evidence_signal: On 22 held-out manipulation tasks, success rose from 28.6% after the first practice round to 95.0% after 15 rounds, and the frozen system achieved 30/30 successes in physical trials after calibration and hardware adaptation.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on good simulator fidelity, dataset coverage, and a robust calibration/adaptation step, performance may degrade when tasks or hardware differ significantly from the practice setting.
paper_title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
